summary: The text argues against limiting or sunsetting the E-Rate program, emphasizing the essential role of broadband in schools and the potential negative impact of reducing screen time on the program.

claims.argument: Limiting E-Rate could lead to higher costs for schools
claims.evidence_quote: Efforts to reduce screen time may have their own merits, but that should have no bearing on the E-Rate program. Broadband is essential to the most basic of school functionalities, and reducing screen time does not translate to lowering broadband costs.
